subject: chemistry

items.q: How do addition and condensation polymerisation differ?
items.correct: Addition joins C=C monomers with no by-product; condensation loses a small molecule (e.g. water).
items.why: Addition polymers form from unsaturated monomers; condensation polymers (e.g. polyesters) eliminate a small molecule as they join.

items.correct: A long chain of many repeating monomer units.
items.why: Many monomers join to form a macromolecule — the polymer.

items.q: Do all plastics behave the same when heated?
items.correct: No — thermoplastics soften and remould; thermosets don't remelt.
items.misconception: Yes, every plastic melts and remoulds.
items.random_wrong: No polymer can ever be recycled.
items.why: Thermoplastics have weak intermolecular forces (remouldable); thermosets are cross-linked and char instead.
